identity.title: Ascending symmetric limb weakness with absent/reduced reflexes (after recent GI/URI illness)

technique.how: Test power in all four limbs proximally and distally (MRC grades) comparing sides, then elicit biceps, triceps, knee and ankle reflexes with reinforcement. Ask about onset (hours-days, progressive over <=4 weeks), distal paresthesias, and diarrhoea or respiratory illness in the preceding 1-4 weeks. Check facial strength, sensory level, and bladder function.
technique.prerequisites: Reflex hammer; patient able to cooperate with power testing; baseline vital capacity or single breath count.

interpretation.positive_finding: Bilateral, relatively symmetric flaccid limb weakness with decreased or absent reflexes in the weak limbs, progressing over days to <=4 weeks, often after a preceding infection, fits Guillain-Barre syndrome (Brighton level 1-3 criteria). Reflexes were reduced initially in 91% and eventually in all of 494 GBS patients.
interpretation.negative_finding: Preserved reflexes do not exclude GBS (9% normal at first exam, 2% persistently) but should prompt consideration of myopathy, hypokalemia/hypophosphatemia or early cord compression; a sensory level, sphincter dysfunction, or asymmetric weakness argues against GBS.
interpretation.pitfalls: Hyperreflexia occurs in some axonal (AMAN) cases; CSF protein is normal in half in the first days; weakness restricted to legs (6%) or arms (1%) occurs; hypokalemic paralysis and botulism mimic the ascending pattern.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: measure vital capacity/SBC, cardiac monitoring, urgent neurology and consider IVIG/plasma exchange; negative: check K/PO4, CK and image the spine if a level is present.

estimates.population: 494 adults with GBS previously enrolled in Dutch therapeutic and observational studies (case series, no non-GBS controls)
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis of GBS by the treating neurologist for study enrolment (NINDS criteria era)
estimates.quote: Decreased reflexes in paretic arms or legs were found initially in 91% of patients and in all patients during follow-up

estimates.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis of GBS by the treating neurologist for study enrolment
estimates.quote: All patients developed bilateral limb weakness which generally involved both upper and lower extremities

sources.citation: Fokke C, van den Berg B, Drenthen J, Walgaard C, van Doorn PA, Jacobs BC. Diagnosis of Guillain-Barre syndrome and validation of Brighton criteria. Brain. 2014;137(Pt 1):33-43.

Sejvar JJ, Kohl KS, Gidudu J, et al. Guillain-Barre syndrome and Fisher syndrome: case definitions and guidelines for collection, analysis, and presentation of immunization safety data. Vaccine. 2011;29(3):599-612.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use reflex status alone to exclude GBS in a patient with rapidly progressive weakness; and do not diagnose GBS when a sensory level, early bladder dysfunction or marked asymmetry suggests cord compression (needs urgent MRI).
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Bulbar weakness, single breath count <20 or vital capacity <20 mL/kg, or autonomic instability (labile BP, arrhythmia) mandate ICU-level monitoring for impending respiratory failure.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Reflex grading and symmetry judgments are examiner-dependent; the 91% figure comes from treating neurologists at first examination, not blinded raters.

extraction_notes: No diagnostic-accuracy study with non-GBS controls was found for the composite finding; the only numbers are feature frequencies (sensitivity-type) within a 494-patient GBS cohort (Fokke 2014, PMID 24163275, abstract): decreased reflexes initially 91% (all during follow-up), bilateral limb weakness 100%, nadir within 4 weeks 97%. Specificity and LRs are therefore null and the record is partially_quantified. Diagnostic criteria (symmetric flaccid weakness, decreased/absent reflexes, monophasic course, nadir <=4 weeks) are consensus from the Brighton Collaboration case definition (Sejvar 2011, PMID 20600491). The Brain full text (Tables) is not open access here. The 'after recent GI/URI illness' element is a risk-factor history, not quantified in this record.
